notes: Rav-Kav card; buses and light rail (since 2023); bikes and scooters are everywhere. The airport train takes 15 minutes (on Shabbat, from Friday evening to Saturday evening, it does NOT run: take a taxi). Train to Haifa.
Winter is 15-20°C, rainy but with sunny days too. April-May and October are ideal; check the dates of Pesach and Yom Kippur (everything closes).
SAFETY: The regional situation changes; check official travel advisories, use the Home Front Command app and follow shelter instructions.
Hummus 35-50 ILS, falafel 20-25, breakfast 50-70, restaurant 120-180; an expensive city, tip 12-15% (cash preferred). Cards are accepted everywhere.
Shabbat: from Friday sunset to Saturday evening most places close, but the beach, Jaffa and restaurants stay open; markets are liveliest on Friday morning.
Buses 405/480 to Jerusalem take 1 hour (not on Shabbat); a day trip is possible.

stops.name: Jaffa Port
stops.tips: A 4,000-year-old port: fishing boats and the Tel Aviv skyline, best in the morning.

stops.name: Old Jaffa Kedumim Square
stops.tips: Stone alleys, St Peter's Church, the zodiac streets and the Hanging Orange Tree.

stops.name: Abu Hassan Ali Karavan
stops.tips: Israel's most famous hummus, 50 years running. Come before noon (it closes when it sells out); tables are shared.

stops.name: Jaffa Flea Market Shuk HaPishpeshim
stops.tips: Antiques, vintage and design. Open Sunday to Thursday, closes at 14:00 on Friday; cafes nearby.

stops.name: Jaffa Beach & Charles Clore Park
stops.tips: Walk the seafront from Jaffa to Tel Aviv at sunset.

backups.name: Dr. Shakshuka
backups.tips: Libyan-style shakshuka; opens at 08:00, in Jaffa.

backups.name: Ilana Goor Museum
backups.tips: The artist's 18th-century house and museum; the rooftop has sea views.

stops.name: Carmel Market Shuk HaCarmel
stops.tips: The city's biggest market: sabich, halva, fresh juice. Liveliest on Friday.

stops.name: Rothschild Boulevard
stops.tips: The Bauhaus boulevard of the UNESCO White City; Independence Hall (1948) and kiosk cafes.

stops.name: Bauhaus Center Tel Aviv
stops.tips: On Dizengoff: a map of the 4,000 Bauhaus buildings and a Friday tour.

stops.name: Miznon Ibn Gabirol
stops.tips: Eyal Shani's pita shop: whole roasted cauliflower, street-food style.

stops.name: Dizengoff Square
stops.tips: Agam's Fire and Water fountain; cafes.

backups.name: Port Sa'id
backups.tips: A hip restaurant opposite the Great Synagogue; records and meze.

backups.name: Independence Hall
backups.tips: The hall where the Declaration of Independence was read; book ahead.

stops.name: Gordon Beach
stops.tips: A winter seafront walk at 18°C; surfers.

stops.name: Tel Aviv Port Namal
stops.tips: A wooden deck in the old port; farmers' market on Friday.

stops.name: Shuk HaNamal Port Market
stops.tips: An indoor gourmet market: fish and cheese.

stops.name: Yarkon Park
stops.tips: The city's Central Park: cycling, rowing boats, a tropical garden.

stops.name: Banana Beach Sunset
stops.tips: Beach bar and seafront sunset over the Mediterranean.

backups.name: Hilton Beach
backups.tips: A gay-friendly surf beach; an alternative to Gordon.

stops.name: Neve Tzedek
stops.tips: The first neighbourhood, founded in 1887: Shabazi Street boutiques and the Suzanne Dellal dance centre.

stops.name: Dallal Bakery
stops.tips: A bakery-cafe in Neve Tzedek; try the croissant.

stops.name: Florentin Street Art
stops.tips: The graffiti district; spices at Levinsky Market.

stops.name: Levinsky Market Café Levinsky 41
stops.tips: Gazoz (homemade fruit soda) and the spice market; Balkan börek.

stops.name: Sarona Market
stops.tips: A gourmet market in the German Templar colony; Anita ice cream.

backups.name: Nahalat Binyamin Bar Evening Teder
backups.tips: A courtyard bar with a radio station; Florentin at night.

backups.name: Nahum Gutman Museum
backups.tips: The painter of Neve Tzedek; an alternative to Florentin.

stops.name: Caesarea National Park
stops.tips: 45 minutes by train plus a bus or tour. Herod's Roman harbour, hippodrome and theatre, and the aqueduct beach.

stops.name: Bahá'í Gardens Haifa
stops.tips: UNESCO gardens in 19 terraces on Mount Carmel. The view from the upper entrance is free (guided tour at 12:00); the German Colony is below.

stops.name: Haifa German Colony Fattoush
stops.tips: In the Arab-Christian neighbourhood on Ben Gurion Boulevard; meze.

stops.name: Acre Old City
stops.tips: The Crusader underground city (Hospitaller fortress, 50 ILS), the Ottoman market and harbour, and the Turkish bath museum.

stops.name: Uri Buri Akko
stops.tips: A world-famous fish restaurant; booking essential. Then the train back.

backups.name: Hummus Said Akko
backups.tips: Legendary hummus in Acre's market; sells out by midday.

backups.name: Rosh Hanikra
backups.tips: A cable car to sea caves on the Lebanese border; an alternative to Acre.

stops.name: Tel Aviv Museum of Art
stops.tips: A building like shattered crystal: Israeli and modern art, Lichtenstein, free on Tuesday evening.

stops.name: ANU Museum of the Jewish People
stops.tips: A museum of the Diaspora at Tel Aviv University; interactive.

stops.name: HaKosem Falafel
stops.tips: The city's best falafel and sabich, on Shlomo HaMelech.

stops.name: Ben Gurion House
stops.tips: The prime minister's home and his 20,000 books; free.

stops.name: Shabbat Dinner Ha'achim
stops.tips: Restaurants fill up on Friday evening: charcoal grills; book ahead.

backups.name: Eretz Israel Museum
backups.tips: Archaeology and glass; next to ANU.

backups.name: Dizengoff Center Food Market
backups.tips: A food market inside the mall on Thursday and Friday.

stops.name: Frishman Beach Morning
stops.tips: A morning swim or run on an empty beach.

stops.name: Café Xoho
stops.tips: Breakfast and bakery; on Gordon.

stops.name: Ben Yehuda Street Souvenirs
stops.tips: Dead Sea cosmetics and tahini to take home.

stops.name: HaHagana Train Ben Gurion
stops.tips: The train to the airport takes 15 minutes (none on Shabbat: on Saturday a taxi costs 150 ILS). Farewell.

backups.name: Sarona Gardens Morning
backups.tips: The Templar garden; an alternative to souvenirs.
